rounds.analysis:
Only iso_3.15 is measured (KL 0.43614, E514ab09c524e). It sits about 213k bits under budget, while an MLP upgrade costs about 3.17M bits. All tabled moves have a positive predicted delta, so single-cell swaps are exhausted under the knapsack. Loss is spread across many MLP layers, and the measured KL is above the single-layer sum.

The untested levers are the GPTQ-family options. Two of them leave stored bits unchanged:
- act_order
- damp, tested in both directions because activation kurtosis is high and the direction is unknown

group_size is the only option that can fund upgrades. Assuming group overhead is (16+nbits)/group_size, which matches the bits deltas in the analysis, rht_gptq_int3 at group_size=256 saves about 0.074 bits per weight across 109 cells. By my estimate that pays for the four most efficient MLP upgrades. The estimate does not use exact parameter counts, so this grid could still be refused as over budget, and the KL cost of the larger groups is unmeasured.

proposals.name: opt_act_order
proposals.rationale: The base iso_3.15 measured KL 0.436144 [E514ab09c524e], with most cells in the GPTQ family. Layers carrying the most loss have highly uneven input channels: model.layers.27.mlp.up_proj has activation channel_absmax_ratio 65.2425 [E3c29dce14bae] and activation kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a]. This grid sets weight_algo.act_order=true on all GPTQ-family methods to process high-activation columns first, with no cell changes.

proposals.name: opt_damp_high
proposals.rationale: The base iso_3.15 measured validation KL 0.436144 [E514ab09c524e]. Activations at model.layers.27.mlp.up_proj are heavy-tailed, with kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a] and absmax 520.657 [E17ce1bbeaa4a] against rms 3.49706 [Ecdb1e7f1288f]. This grid tests whether stronger regularization of the calibration Hessian, damp=0.03, generalizes better to validation windows. Stored bits do not change.

proposals.name: opt_damp_low
proposals.rationale: This grid brackets the damping direction from the other side, against the base iso_3.15 at KL 0.436144 [E514ab09c524e]. Loss concentrates in low-bit cells such as model.layers.14.mlp.down_proj under rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633466 [E4c3f9b73e065], where error compensation matters most. damp=0.002 gives the Hessian-weighted compensation more strength, and stored bits do not change.

proposals.name: g256_rht3_mlp_upgrades

Single-layer table KL for each upgrade: model.layers.14.mlp.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 0.00633466 [E4c3f9b73e065] to rht_gptq_int3 0.00181478 [E90bd4b2f3645]; model.layers.3.mlp.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.0064177 [E6f4f7ea296d5] to gptq_int4 0.00237732 [Ef4ee8cb4969e]; model.layers.2.mlp.up_proj gptq_int3 0.00641875 [E9baa10763ebe] to gptq_int4 0.00237045 [Ef3d9c7b4502c]; model.layers.1.mlp.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.00611131 [E0564bc6ad1eb] to rht_gptq_int4 0.00227173 [E779bc065b72e]. The KL cost of the larger groups has not been measured, and this grid tests whether the upgrades outweigh it.

rounds.analysis: All four grids from last round were refused because a truncated KL value was cited, so no options have been measured yet. Bits per weight implied by bits_delta_per_weight fit n + (16+n)/group_size at the default group size. For the budget, 28 blocks of 15 units of 2^20 weights give 420 units, which matches the method mix and leaves only 13/64 unit-bits of slack. An int3 to int4 swap costs exactly what an int3 to int2 downgrade saves, and the retrieved layers show int2 is very costly, so swaps at fixed options look unattractive. Three grids therefore test GPTQ options one at a time at no bit cost. The fourth buys upgrades by raising group_size on the whole GPTQ family. Assuming the same overhead formula holds at group_size 256, savings are at least 26 unit-bits even if all 17 non-GPTQ cells were MLP layers, against about 24 unit-bits for the 8 MLP upgrades. The KL penalty of the larger group size is unmeasured, and this grid will show whether the upgrades outweigh it.
